steps.why: Write the item down. Capture records it and stops.
Build it in small commits. The proof gate needs a red run, then a green one.
Review the branch, then open the PR or merge.

title: Fix a small bug or add a small feature
when: One clear item, small enough to build in one sitting.

steps.why: Record the feature as an item.
Settle the design with you, section by section.
Turn the design into tasks with a way to verify each.
Build the plan, one verified task at a time.
Review against what the item promised, then merge.

title: Build a bigger feature
when: A Major item where the design or the approach needs sign-off before code lands.

steps.why: Reproduce it, test one hypothesis at a time, fix it in one commit.
Review and merge the fix.
Keep what the bug taught you for the next session.

title: Chase a bug you don't understand
when: Something is broken and the cause is not known yet.

steps.why: Try it on a throwaway branch. Only the findings come back.
Plan the real work with what the spike found.
Build it.

title: Try a risky idea first
when: You don't know yet whether an approach or a library works.

steps.why: Suggest config values from the repo, confirmed one by one.
Turn the brief into milestones.
Plan the first milestone slice.
Turn the plan into backlog items.
Build the first item.

title: Start a project from a brief
when: An empty repo and an idea of where it should go.

steps.why: Shape the slate so every issue has clear acceptance.
Hand issues to workers, review their PRs, merge through the gate.
Answer the decisions the round put to you, one at a time.
At wind-down, keep what the round learned.
Cut a release when the work adds up to one.

title: Run several issues in parallel
when: A few independent issues are ready and you can stay around for questions.

steps.why: Save the lessons worth keeping.
Write a handoff so a fresh session continues.
Next session, with no argument, it reads the handoff and picks up.

title: Stop for today
when: The context is filling up or you have to leave mid-item.
